boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Nebraska traditions spanning Memorial Stadium, student honors, music, and campus history.

cards.title: Enter with the Tunnel Walk
cards.subtitle: Memorial Stadium pregame
cards.notes: Watch the Cornhuskers emerge from the northeast tunnel before a home game, with the stadium video sequence and “Sirius” framing the entrance.
cards.short_summary: Nebraska’s signature football-team entrance unfolds from the Memorial Stadium tunnel.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL Archives describes the Tunnel Walk as a Nebraska football tradition in which the Cornhuskers emerge from the North tunnel to “Sirius” at the beginning of games.
cards.source_title: Husker Legacy Statue · The Monuments of Memorial Stadium
cards.access_notes: Observe from a ticketed home football game; follow current Athletics entry and event policies.

cards.title: Make the Class “N”
cards.subtitle: Big Red Welcome at Memorial Stadium
cards.notes: Incoming students walk onto Memorial Stadium’s field during Big Red Welcome, then gather for a class photo in a giant N formation.
cards.short_summary: A first-year welcome ritual lets new students take their own version of the Tunnel Walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Nebraska Today reported that the Class of 2027 completed its own Tunnel Walk and formed a giant N on Memorial Stadium’s field.
cards.source_title: New Huskers celebrate with Tunnel Walk, convocation
cards.access_notes: This is part of Big Red Welcome programming for new students; consult the current welcome schedule for eligibility.

cards.title: Recognize the Blackshirts
cards.subtitle: Nebraska football defense
cards.notes: Look for the black practice jerseys associated with Nebraska’s defense, a designation traced by UNL Archives to Coach Bob Devaney’s 1963 team.
cards.short_summary: The defense’s black-jersey identity is one of the program’s long-running visual traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL Archives states that Nebraska’s defense has been known as the Blackshirts since Bob Devaney put the unit in black pullover practice jerseys in 1963.
cards.source_title: Husker Legacy Statue · The Monuments of Memorial Stadium
cards.access_notes: A football-program tradition; roster and practice recognition are determined by Nebraska Athletics.

cards.title: Trace Ivy Day’s Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Historic UNL spring observance
cards.notes: Explore the university history of Ivy Day, a spring ceremony that brought together honors recognition, student organizations, and ceremonial planting.
cards.short_summary: Ivy Day is a historic campus observance with roots in UNL’s early twentieth-century student life.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL’s institutional history says the first Ivy Day was held in 1901 and that the tradition endured through the ceremonial planting of ivy.
cards.access_notes: This card documents a historic university tradition; availability of any current ceremony should be confirmed with its organizers.

cards.title: Spot the Sunglasses “Shading”
cards.subtitle: Innocents Society initiation
cards.notes: Learn why new Innocents receive sunglasses: UNL replaced its former physical selection ritual with a safer “shading” initiation.
cards.short_summary: Sunglasses now mark selection into UNL’s historic Chancellor’s Senior Honorary.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL’s history page says the Innocents Society discontinued tackling because of injuries and now initiates new members through “shading,” presenting them with sunglasses.
cards.access_notes: An honorary-society initiation, not a public participation activity; do not imitate the discontinued tackling practice.

cards.title: Notice the Black Masque Tap
cards.subtitle: Mortar Board’s UNL lineage
cards.notes: Connect Mortar Board’s campus chapter to its Black Masque predecessor, whose members initiated new members through a ceremonial tap.
cards.short_summary: A historic tapping ritual links UNL’s Black Masque chapter to today’s Mortar Board.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL’s history page states that Black Masque initiated members by “tapping” and later became affiliated with the national Mortar Board organization.
cards.access_notes: An honorary-society tradition; participation is limited to the organization’s selected members.

cards.title: Remember the Victory Bell
cards.subtitle: Discontinued Nebraska–Missouri rivalry ritual
cards.notes: See the Victory Bell as a piece of rivalry history: the Innocents Society exchanged it with Missouri’s QEBH Society until conference realignment ended it.
cards.short_summary: Nebraska retained the bell after the student-society exchange concluded in 2010.
cards.evidence_claim: A UNL announcement says the Innocents Society’s Victory Bell exchange with Missouri’s QEBH Society began in 1927, ended after the 2010 season, and left Nebraska with the bell.
cards.access_notes: Discontinued tradition; this card is for historical context, not participation.

cards.title: Join “Hail Varsity”
cards.subtitle: Official Nebraska school song
cards.notes: Follow the Cornhusker Marching Band’s posted lyrics for “Hail Varsity,” Nebraska’s official school song since 1937.
cards.short_summary: The university’s official school song began as a 1936 Kosmet Klub revue number.
cards.evidence_claim: UNL history records that “Hail Varsity” debuted in 1936 and became an official school song in 1937; the band publishes its current lyrics.
cards.access_notes: The Cornhusker Marching Band provides current fight-song information online.

cards.entity_name: Cornhusker Marching Band Pregame Rear Back
cards.title: Catch the Pregame Rear Back
cards.subtitle: Cornhusker Marching Band at Memorial Stadium
cards.notes: Watch the marching band’s pregame routine for the rear back, a traditional move performed while players high-step and angle instruments upward.
cards.short_summary: A visually distinctive band move is woven into Nebraska’s stadium pregame.
cards.evidence_claim: Nebraska Today identified the rear back as a traditional Cornhusker Marching Band move retained in the pregame routine.
cards.source_title: Cornhusker Marching Band revamps pregame routine
cards.access_notes: Observe during a ticketed Memorial Stadium football event; performance details may vary by season.

cards.title: Listen for the Accordion Guy
cards.subtitle: Husker home-football game days
cards.notes: Keep an ear out for Chris Sayre’s accordion performance on home game days; his long-running set commonly includes “No Place Like Nebraska” and “Hail Varsity.”
cards.short_summary: An accordion player has become a documented part of Nebraska home-game-day atmosphere since 1982.
cards.evidence_claim: Nebraska Today reports that Chris Sayre began playing on Husker home football game days in 1982 and that fans request traditional Nebraska songs.
cards.source_title: After 43 years, Sayre still squeezin’ his way through Husker game days
cards.access_notes: Public game-day performance; its exact location and appearance can vary by home game.
